name: PageContentHeader
intent: Route-content header that unifies identity or page title, optional peer navigation, status metadata, priority actions, accessible overflow, and split-primary workflows.
when: A route inside an existing application shell needs a title or entity identity plus actions
The same product needs consistent navigation, entity-action, and title-action header variants
Secondary actions must collapse to an accessible overflow while the title and primary action remain visible
whenNot: The persistent application shell needs sidebar pairing, project switching, global search, notifications, and identity -> use CoreAppTopBar with CoreAppSidebar
A complete organization/project dashboard shell header is required -> use CoreDashboardHeader
A small contextual row above a canvas or panel is sufficient -> use ContextToolbar

chooseOver.because: PageContentHeader is route-local content; CoreDashboardHeader owns a complete dashboard shell context.

insteadUse.whenInstead: The header must own organization/project switching, global search, notifications, identity, and dashboard context tabs.
The surface only needs a compact context label, status, and a small action set.

states.navigation: Entity identity, peer ViewTabBar, and action hierarchy
states.entity-actions: Entity identity/status with primary, secondary, and overflow actions
states.title-actions: Page title/description with supporting controls and optional split-primary action
states.responsive: Secondary controls collapse into overflow and navigation moves to a dedicated row below desktop width
states.titleScale: The title steps DOWN as the header narrows rather than holding a desktop size in a phone-width column: title-actions runs 24px only once the header has the width for it, 20px at @md and 18px below. Sizes read off the header's own @container, not the viewport, because a header inside a 380px panel on a wide screen is narrow whatever the window says. The size and weight are !important on purpose — this is a semantic heading, our utilities live in @layer utilities, and ANY unlayered `h1 {}` rule in a host app beats a layered one however specific it is; styles.tw4.css ships no reset by design, so preflight cannot be relied on to have zeroed it either.
states.disabled: Individual actions and split options honor their disabled state

allowedPlacement: Direct child of route content below the application shell
Top of a detail, workspace, playground, or operational route
forbiddenPlacement: As a replacement for the persistent application shell top bar
Inside a table row or small card
Nested inside another PageContentHeader or CoreDashboardHeader

commonMistakes.mistake: Passing navigation tabs without variant="navigation" and controlled activeTab/onTabChange props
commonMistakes.symptom: The peer navigation is not rendered
commonMistakes.fix: Use the navigation variant and provide tabs, activeTab, and onTabChange together.

commonMistakes.symptom: The header has no clear action hierarchy and cannot collapse gracefully
commonMistakes.fix: Keep one primary workflow, leave supporting actions secondary, and mark rare actions overflow.

minimalExample: <PageContentHeader variant="title-actions" title="Playground" description="Iterate on and test prompts." actions={[{id: "evaluation", label: "Set up Evaluation", onSelect: setup}]} splitAction={{id: "start", label: "Start", onSelect: start, options: [{id: "template", label: "From template", onSelect: fromTemplate}]}} />

evaluationCriteria.check: Selected for route content, never as an application shell substitute.
All visible controls are rendered by Core ViewTabBar, Button, ButtonGroup, DropdownMenu, and Tooltip artifacts.
At desktop and narrow widths, title and primary action remain visible, secondary actions stay accessible from overflow, and groups never overlap.
Peer navigation, direct actions, overflow actions, and split action options are keyboard accessible and invoke their handlers.

ownership.expectedWrapper: Direct route-content child without duplicate background, divider, height, or horizontal padding.

lineage.confidence: high — three reference variants mapped to existing Core artifacts
